youtube.title: France tried a 10-hour day and it failed ⏳ #Shorts
youtube.description:
We count money, distance and weight in tens. Everything except time. In 1793, revolutionary France tried to fix that with a ten-hour day and a hundred minutes in every hour. It lasted less than two years. Clockmakers built dual dials, but people would have had to replace every clock and watch they owned, and their lives already ran on the old hours. Ten was easier to count, but sixty was easier to share. Full episode on the channel.
